title: S2RL: Do We Really Need to Perceive All States in Deep Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning?

problem.claim: Decentralized MARL agents must model local utility functions from their own observations, but local observations contain entities with differing and time-varying importance.

gap.claim: Existing methods treat each local observation as a whole, and existing attention models rely on dense fully connected graphs that do not better perceive important states.

contributions.claim: A sparse state based MARL framework, S2RL, uses sparse attention to discard irrelevant information in local observations.
S2RL estimates local utility functions with self-attention and sparse attention separately, then combines them into standard and auxiliary joint value functions in the central critic.
S2RL is designed as a plug-and-play module applicable to various methods.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on StarCraft II.
The authors report that S2RL significantly improves the performance of many state-of-the-art methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Collaborative MARL is used in practical applications with agents making decisions from their own observations.
Mainstream methods model each local observation as a whole despite entity-level and time-varying relevance.
Existing attention approaches use dense fully connected graphs and do not better perceive important states.
S2RL applies sparse attention and combines separate utility estimates into joint value functions.
The authors report improved performance across many state-of-the-art methods in StarCraft II experiments.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the sparse attention construction or selection rule.
The abstract does not identify the evaluated state-of-the-art methods or report quantitative results.
The abstract does not describe computational costs, ablations, or implementation details.
